subject: financial-literacy
title: Launch and diagnostic: needs, wants, and priorities
standards: Michigan Personal Finance foundations — introductory
Grade 4 economics and mathematics connections
Manuel Academy Financial Literacy elementary sequence — Grade 4
Manuel Academy Financial Literacy G4 Unit 1 — choices, scarcity, and tradeoffs
essential_question: How do I make a money choice on purpose instead of by accident?
learning_objectives: Activate prior knowledge about needs, wants, and priorities, surface initial thinking without penalty, and establish the unit question.
Use age-appropriate evidence, a model, or a demonstration to communicate understanding of needs, wants, and priorities.
Check, revise, or improve work about needs, wants, and priorities using the stated success criteria.
success_criteria: The learner completes the central task about needs, wants, and priorities.
The learner gives evidence, reasoning, a model, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer.
The learner checks or revises the work and can name one next step.
materials: course notebook or digital equivalent
pencil or accessible response tool
play money, counters, or a printable simulated money set
printable or on-screen planning chart for simulated amounts

lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Present a brief, accessible prompt connected to “needs, wants, and priorities.” Ask the learner to notice, predict, recall, or pose a question before instruction.

Model one simulated money decision end to end: read the situation, compare the options, name the tradeoff, record the simulated figures, and check the total. Keep the explanation centered on needs, wants, and priorities. Use fictional amounts only, name the success criteria, and model how to check the work.
Complete two supported examples or tasks about needs, wants, and priorities. After each step, ask: “What tells you that step is right?” Fade prompts on the second example.
Learner completes a new application of needs, wants, and priorities and records both the result and the reasoning, evidence, process, or design choice that produced it.
In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about needs, wants, and priorities; then identify one check that would catch an error, a wrong total, or a weak claim.

student_activity: Learner completes a new application of needs, wants, and priorities and records both the result and the reasoning, evidence, process, or design choice that produced it.
formative_check: In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about needs, wants, and priorities; then identify one check that would catch an error, a wrong total, or a weak claim.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score the stated learning target, the reasoning about the simulated situation, the accuracy of the simulated figures, and the revision. Accept multiple valid approaches when they meet the criteria. Express any simulated tax or interest as a stated flat amount or a whole-cent add-on per simulated dollar; percentages, decimal operations, and fraction operations are not required at this grade. Do not score family income, household spending, or personal circumstances. Do not infer effort, motivation, diagnosis, or character from an error.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for needs, wants, and priorities, model it with a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item.
Ask the learner to explain, draw, or demonstrate why the process for needs, wants, and priorities works before continuing.
Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of needs, wants, and priorities, and avoid unnecessary remediation.
Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review.
Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking needs, wants, and priorities mastered.

mastery_rule: Do not mark mastery from one answer. Use a checklist, drawing, planning page, simulated record, learner explanation, or another no-photo artifact; require accurate independent evidence and successful transfer or retrieval on at least two occasions when feasible. Simulated practice, marketplace play, and budget games record completion only and do not by themselves advance official mastery; official mastery requires independent explanation and application evidence on a later or different occasion.
extension: Apply needs, wants, and priorities to a new simulated situation, compare two simulated approaches, or teach the idea with an original make-believe example. Do not complete another learner's graded work and do not use real financial information.
accessibility_and_accommodations: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
safety_and_privacy: Use respectful, no-shame language. Family income, spending, debt, and financial circumstances are never compared, ranked, scored, or requested.
Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Every amount, price, wage, budget, account, and business in this course is fictional and simulated. No real money moves at any point.
Never request, collect, display, or record real bank data, account numbers, balances, card numbers, PINs, passwords, or tax identifiers.
This course teaches general concepts only. It never gives individualized financial, tax, credit, insurance, or investment advice to a learner or a family.
No purchase, real account, subscription, app download, or real transaction is required to complete any lesson, project, or assessment.
No identifiable learner photo is required. Accept a checklist, drawing, planning page, learner explanation, or guardian confirmation instead.
Reflection may be kept private. No learner is required to disclose family finances, household circumstances, or personal history.
Teach that passwords, account details, and money information are kept private and shared only with a trusted adult, never with a stranger or an app.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, simulated price chart, play-money model, worked example, or short demonstration supporting needs, wants, and priorities.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile or concrete model, or an adult demonstration.

parent_or_guardian_visibility: Share the lesson target, completion state, evidence type, and next instructional step. Do not expose raw private reflections, raw answers, voice recordings, or diagnosis language. Simulated money work is reported as completion and evidence type only; no real financial data about the learner or the household is collected or displayed.
home_connection: Invite the learner to talk with a trusted adult about one make-believe example of needs, wants, and priorities. No purchase, real account, card, balance, photograph, or family financial information is required or requested.

safety_and_privacy: Use respectful, no-shame language. Family income, spending, debt, and financial circumstances are never compared, ranked, scored, or requested.
